difficulty_reason: The proof controls an exact induced edge count without any regularity or independence of the hypergraph edges. It defines a normalized distribution on extendable ordered vertex sequences, classifies last-vertex link families, and bounds all prefix-extension denominators through forbidden completions. Averaging over label permutations produces an exponential gain whose optimization gives the universal one-over-e factor. The complete original new core is explicit; supporting elementary estimates and helper statements are not separate units.
scope_text: Only the complete original Theorem 1.4, selected for positive integers \(r\ge3,k,\ell\) with \(1\le\ell<k/r\): \(\operatorname{ind}_r(k,\ell)\le\operatorname{ind}_{\le r}(k,\ell)\le k/(k-r\ell)/e\). The original all-positive-r statement remains intact. Edges are nonempty; inducibility is the limit as \(n\) tends to infinity of the maximum induced-edge probability. This is not an exact finite-n probability bound. The entire Section 2 good-sequence weighting, normalization, link-class and permutation/AM-GM argument and authored calculus closure are selected. The graph conjecture and later concentration results remain unselected context, never separate units.
